title: Exercise: Scale a 4 to 20 mA Pressure Signal
oneLiner: Convert raw analog counts into bar with REAL arithmetic, clamp the range, and flag a broken wire instead of reporting zero pressure.
keyTakeaway: Convert to REAL, subtract the 4 mA count, multiply by the engineering span and divide by the count span; check for wire break first and clamp the rest.
explanation:
A pressure transmitter sends 4 to 20 mA for 0 to 10 bar, and the analog card turns that current into counts. Write the scaling so the rest of the program can work in bar, and make a dead or disconnected transmitter raise a fault instead of reading as zero pressure.

The card's numbers in this exercise are made up for the purpose; real cards document their own ranges, and many can be configured to scale the value for you.
